### ITERATION 1 CONSTRAINTS
[A-Section]: When detailing potential etiologies or contributing factors, only include those explicitly stated by the provider or directly supported by the transcript as part of the clinical assessment. Avoid inferring causal relationships between patient habits (e.g., caffeine intake) and primary complaints (e.g., pain) unless explicitly stated by the provider as a diagnostic finding.

### ITERATION 2 CONSTRAINTS
[A-Section]: For etiologies and contributing factors, strictly limit to relationships explicitly stated by the provider. Do not infer causal links between patient habits (e.g., caffeine) and primary complaints (e.g., pain) if the provider attributes the habit to a different outcome (e.g., caffeine to sleep quality) or does not explicitly link it to the complaint.

### ITERATION 3 CONSTRAINTS
[A-Section]: Etiologies and contributing factors must be *explicitly stated by the provider* as directly related to the primary complaint. Do not infer causal links from patient habits (e.g., caffeine) to the primary complaint (e.g., pain) if the provider attributes the habit to a different outcome (e.g., sleep quality) or does not explicitly establish the connection in the assessment.
